intent:
I am telling Mike the facts, but I am leaving out how close I came to running outside after Dad. I had my hand on the door before I remembered Mrs. Dempsey and what one mistake inside this house can cost. I am frightened by how quickly seeing Dad overpowered every survival instinct I had developed.

Dad’s route to the window matters. He used to stop there after working late because the workshop light was visible from that side of the property. He would check whether I was still awake before walking around to the front. Seeing him repeat that pattern makes me believe memory is operating underneath the infection.

I need Mike to help me turn the house into a controlled retrieval point. I can use the workshop light, speakers, radios, and sounds from Dad’s old tools to draw him back without immediately opening the door. Mike can watch the road, monitor the woods, and tell me whether Dad is traveling alone.

The early-stage restriction makes every hour feel expensive. I need to know where Dad went and how quickly he is changing. I want Mike’s help, but I am also trying to prevent him from realizing that I may go searching alone if Dad does not return soon.
emotion: urgent, shaken, practical, and barely restraining reckless hope
